documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT CARDIOLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit date: 11/07/2024
Referring: Internal Medicine - Primary Care

Ms. Friedman is a 45-year-old high school mathematics teacher seen today at the request of her primary care physician for episodic symptoms.

History of present illness
Over the past several weeks she has had spells that arrive without warning. Each begins with a sensation of her heart racing in her chest, followed by a pounding headache and flushing. The episodes last several minutes and resolve spontaneously. Between them she feels more fatigued than is normal for her and her sleep has at times been poor. She denies chest pain. She has noticed no change in her vision and has not lost weight.

Past history: no chronic medical illness. Tonsillectomy 1995. Cesarean section 2015.
Medications: none.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: her father died in his 40s of what the family described as a "thyroid problem"; no records are available to her.
Social: never smoker; alcohol one to two drinks per week; works as a high school math teacher.

Examination
Seated blood pressure 120/76 mmHg. On rising from the chair to standing, blood pressure measured 198/102 mmHg.
Alert, comfortable. JVP not elevated. Carotids without bruit. Regular rhythm with normal first and second heart sounds, no murmur, rub or extra sound. Lung fields clear. Abdomen soft. No peripheral edema; distal pulses full.

Data
ECG today: normal sinus rhythm, normal intervals, no repolarization abnormality.
Chest radiograph today: no acute cardiopulmonary findings, normal heart size.
Laboratory: basic metabolic panel, CBC and TSH within normal limits. Plasma free metanephrines elevated.

Impression
1. Paroxysmal hypertension, with a marked pressor response on standing in a patient having discrete adrenergic-type spells.
2. Elevated plasma metanephrines. In this setting pheochromocytoma is suspected.
3. Normal ECG and chest radiograph; no evidence of structural or primary rhythm disease on this evaluation.

Recommendations
- Endocrine evaluation for confirmation and localization of a suspected catecholamine-secreting tumor. We would ask that her primary care office arrange the endocrinology referral.
- Return to cardiology as needed.

Cardiology

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/09/2025

Reason for consultation: palpable anterior neck mass and diarrhea, in a patient with paroxysmal hypertension and elevated plasma metanephrines found by cardiology in 11/2024. Visit moved up at her primary care physician's request.

History
Ms. Friedman is a 46-year-old teacher. She recently found a lump in the front of her neck and has had ongoing diarrhea. Her spells of racing heartbeat, headache and flushing continue.
PMH: paroxysmal hypertension (cardiology 11/2024), elevated plasma metanephrines with suspected pheochromocytoma. No other illness.
PSH: tonsillectomy 1995; cesarean section 2015.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father had thyroid cancer and died in his 40s; a paternal aunt had a pheochromocytoma; mother has hypertension. Taken together, this family pattern is consistent with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A).
Social: never smoker, 1-2 alcoholic drinks weekly, high school mathematics teacher.

Examination
BP 145/90 mmHg, HR 98 bpm.
Thyroid: firm, nontender nodule in the mid-portion of the gland. No cervical lymphadenopathy.
Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender.

Laboratory (today)
Calcium 10.2 mg/dL (reference 8.5-10.2)
Calcitonin 500 pg/mL (reference <10)
CEA 10 ng/mL (reference <5)

Assessment
1. Thyroid nodule with markedly elevated calcitonin and elevated CEA: medullary thyroid carcinoma is suspected.
2. Suspected pheochromocytoma (paroxysmal hypertension, adrenergic spells, elevated plasma metanephrines).
3. Family history pattern of MEN 2A.

Plan
The pheochromocytoma must be confirmed and removed before any thyroid surgery is undertaken; thyroidectomy will follow adrenal surgery.
Ordered:
- Repeat plasma free metanephrines and plasma catecholamines; 24-hour urine catecholamines and fractionated metanephrines.
- CT abdomen with adrenal protocol.
- Thyroid and neck ultrasound.
- Germline RET mutation testing, with referral to genetics for counseling.
We will coordinate the surgical referral once results are back. Copy to primary care.

Endocrinology

events.reason: Genetic counseling and germline RET result

documents.title: Genetics Consultation
documents.author: genetics
documents.body:
CANCER GENETICS - CONSULTATION AND RESULT DISCLOSURE
Date: 06/19/2025
Referred by endocrinology.

Ms. Friedman, 46, met with us in person to review germline RET testing sent by endocrinology. She is being evaluated for a right adrenal mass consistent with pheochromocytoma and a thyroid nodule with elevated calcitonin. Family history as she reports it: father with thyroid cancer, died in his 40s; paternal aunt with pheochromocytoma; mother with hypertension. No relative's genetic testing is known to her.

Result
RET gene, germline: heterozygous pathogenic variant, p.Cys634Arg (codon 634).

Interpretation
This result confirms a diagnosis of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A in Ms. Friedman. Codon 634 variants are associated with a high risk of medullary thyroid carcinoma and of pheochromocytoma, which fits her current presentation.

Counseling provided
- Autosomal dominant inheritance: each first-degree relative has a 50% chance of carrying the same variant.
- Cascade testing is recommended for at-risk blood relatives. We provided a family letter she may share; relatives can be tested through any genetics program.
- Her management is directed by endocrinology and surgery: adrenal surgery first, then thyroidectomy, with lifelong biochemical surveillance afterward.
She had time for questions and was given our direct line.

Medical Genetics

documents.title: General Surgery Preoperative Evaluation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
GENERAL SURGERY - PREOPERATIVE EVALUATION
Date: 11/10/2025

Indication: right adrenal mass, biochemically and radiographically consistent with pheochromocytoma, in a patient with MEN 2A (germline RET p.Cys634Arg). Referred by endocrinology. Planned laparoscopic right adrenalectomy 11/14/2025.

HPI: 46F, back for preoperative evaluation. She was evaluated by cardiology in 11/2024 and by endocrinology in 05/2025 for paroxysmal hypertension, and the right adrenal mass was found during that workup. She now has spells several times a week: a pounding headache together with palpitations and sweating, each lasting about 20 to 30 minutes. Her home cuff has captured readings above 180/100 mmHg during spells; between them her pressures are normal.

PMH: MEN 2A. Paroxysmal hypertension. Thyroid nodule with calcitonin 500 pg/mL and CEA 10 ng/mL (05/2025), suspected medullary thyroid carcinoma - thyroidectomy to follow recovery from adrenal surgery.
PSH: tonsillectomy 1995, cesarean section 2015.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father - medullary thyroid carcinoma diagnosed at age 48. Paternal aunt - pheochromocytoma. Mother - essential hypertension.
SHx: never smoker; social alcohol, 1-2 drinks/week; high school mathematics teacher.

Data
Plasma and urine catecholamines and metanephrines (06/2025): markedly elevated.
CT adrenal protocol (06/03/2025): 3.6 cm heterogeneous right adrenal mass, unenhanced 38 HU; normal left adrenal; no other abdominal mass.

Exam
BP 117/67, HR 65 /min, Wt 64.1 kg.
Well appearing. Neck: firm nodule mid thyroid. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no palpable mass; healed low transverse incision.

Assessment and plan
Right adrenal pheochromocytoma in MEN 2A, symptomatic.
- Admit today to the regional hospital for preoperative preparation.
- Start phenoxybenzamine 10 mg by mouth twice daily. Liberal salt and fluid intake. Seated and standing blood pressure and heart rate each shift.
- Laparoscopic right adrenalectomy 11/14/2025. Risks, benefits and alternatives reviewed; consent signed.
- Thyroid surgery to be scheduled with our group after recovery.

General Surgery

DIAGNOSIS: Right adrenal gland, laparoscopic adrenalectomy - pheochromocytoma, 3.6 cm, confined to the adrenal gland. Margins negative.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (regional hospital, received by fax 11/19/2025)
Admitted: 11/10/2025. Discharged: 11/17/2025.
Admitting diagnosis: right adrenal pheochromocytoma, MEN 2A.
Discharge diagnosis: right adrenal pheochromocytoma, status post laparoscopic right adrenalectomy.

Hospital course
Admitted from the surgical clinic for preoperative preparation. Phenoxybenzamine 10 mg twice daily was started on 11/10. Over the following days her blood pressure came down steadily, without a significant fall on standing, and her palpitations became milder.
On 11/14 she underwent laparoscopic right adrenalectomy without complication. Phenoxybenzamine was stopped after surgery. Postoperatively her blood pressure stayed normal with no antihypertensive medication and she had no further spells. Diet advanced without difficulty; ambulating independently; port sites clean and dry.
Pathology (final 11/17): pheochromocytoma, 3.6 cm, confined to the adrenal gland, margins negative.

Discharge medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb for 2 weeks; may shower. Call for fever, wound redness or drainage, or recurrent spells.
Follow-up: surgical clinic in 2 weeks; primary care in 1-2 weeks; plasma free metanephrines in about one month (ordered by surgery). Thyroid surgery planning with our office and endocrinology.

documents.title: Operative Report - Laparoscopic Right Adrenalectomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT (received with discharge records)
Date of surgery: 11/14/2025
Preoperative diagnosis: right adrenal pheochromocytoma, MEN 2A.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: laparoscopic right adrenalectomy.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal; arterial line placed by anesthesia.
Preparation: phenoxybenzamine 10 mg twice daily since admission 11/10.

Description: Patient positioned left lateral decubitus. Transabdominal laparoscopic approach with four ports in the right subcostal region. The right triangular ligament was divided and the liver retracted medially. The right adrenal vein was identified early, clipped and divided. The adrenal gland, containing the mass, was dissected free from the kidney and the inferior vena cava and removed intact in a retrieval bag. Hemostasis confirmed. Ports closed.
Findings: right adrenal mass approximately 3.6 cm, removed intact. No other abnormality seen.
Estimated blood loss: minimal. Complications: none. Hemodynamics remained stable throughout.
Phenoxybenzamine discontinued after surgery.
Disposition: to PACU, then surgical floor, in stable condition.

General Surgery
